name: FC Shakhtar Donetsk
city: Donetsk (in exile since 2014; domestic home games in Lviv, 2026/27 UCL home games at Stamford Bridge, London)

ucl_2026_27.qualified_via: Ukrainian Premier League 2025/26 champion (16th title; direct entry to league phase)

identity.playing_style: Arda Turan (appointed 27 May 2025 on a two-year deal to summer 2027) plays a 4-3-3 built on possession and territorial dominance, fed by a conveyor belt of young Brazilian technicians (Kauã Elias, Luca Meirelles, Eguinaldo, Pedrinho, Alisson Santana). In 2025/26 the team won the league by 12 points (69 vs LNZ's 57), had a 21-match unbeaten run, and reached the Conference League semi-final (lost to Crystal Palace 1-3 home, 1-2 away) while topping the competition's xG rankings.
principles: buy young Brazilians, develop, sell high (Kevin to Fulham EUR 40m, Sudakov to Benfica EUR 20.25m)
resilience in exile: no home stadium since 2014, neutral-venue European home games since 2022
attacking, possession-based identity regardless of coach
domestic dominance as a platform for European income
owner-funded (Rinat Akhmetov) with a strong Ukrainian core (Riznyk, Bondar, Matviienko, Ocheretko, Bondarenko)
identity.club_character: Privately owned by Rinat Akhmetov; the most successful Ukrainian club of the 21st century. Displaced from the Donbass Arena since 2014 and, since the 2022 full-scale invasion, forced to play European 'home' games abroad (Krakow, now London). Fanbase dispersed across Ukraine and the diaspora; the club is publicly framed as a symbol of national resilience. High but different pressure: expectation to win domestically and to represent Ukraine in Europe.
identity.political_and_social_context: Publicly documented institution-level facts only: (1) Shakhtar has not played at the Donbass Arena since 2014 because of the war in eastern Ukraine; domestic home games are in Lviv (Arena Lviv). (2) UEFA requires Ukrainian clubs to play European home fixtures at neutral venues since 2022; Shakhtar used Krakow and for 2026/27 has agreed with Chelsea to stage UCL home games at Stamford Bridge. (3) Shakhtar sold Kevin to Fulham for a reported club-record EUR 40m and Sudakov to Benfica; Konoplya left for Borussia Mönchengladbach as a free agent. (4) 2025/26 UPL matches drew a league-high 101,050 total attendance despite wartime restrictions.
identity.transfer_policy: buy-to-sell: recruit teenage/early-20s Brazilians and sell at peak (Kevin EUR 40m, Sudakov EUR 20.25m); retain a Ukrainian spine; opportunistic free domestic signings (Karavaev from Dynamo Kyiv)

last_season_2025_26.ucl_result: Not in UCL (lost qualifying route); UEFA Conference League semi-final (lost 2-5 agg to Crystal Palace)

top_scorer.name: Kauã Elias / Luca Meirelles (11 each, all competitions); Eguinaldo / Lassina Traoré (7 each, league)

strengths: Dominant domestically (69 pts, 12-point margin, 21-game unbeaten run) with a settled possession identity.
Deep European run in 2025/26 (Conference League semi-final) and the competition's best xG output, so the young squad has knockout experience.
Production line of saleable Brazilian talent (Kevin EUR 40m, Sudakov EUR 20.25m) keeps the balance sheet healthy without an owner cash call.
Stable, well-established Ukrainian defensive spine (Riznyk, Bondar, Matviienko) under a coach entering his second season.
Playing UCL home games at Stamford Bridge gives a genuine big-stadium stage rather than an empty neutral ground.
weaknesses: Lost two of their most productive attackers (Kevin, Sudakov) and starting right-back Konoplya in one window; only a free 34-year-old (Karavaev) verified as arriving.
Goal spread is thin: top league scorers had only 7 goals each; no proven 15-goal striker.
Very young, mostly Brazilian attack may be exposed against Inter, Real Madrid and Leipzig's intensity.
Logistics of exile (domestic games in Lviv, European games in London) add travel load and remove real home advantage.
Squad 2026/27 only partially verifiable; exact contract lengths and ages missing for most players.
